title: AA Batteries 8-pack

drivers.name: Store closure (Monday)
drivers.evidence: One past week with similar closure: sales dropped 15% vs baseline (2025-03-24, store closed for renovation).

drivers.name: Price increase (5.5%)
drivers.evidence: Same price last week: 31 units (12% below baseline). Noise-adjusted price sensitivity estimate from past promotions: -10% to -15% per 5% price increase.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 35.2. Store closure on Monday (1 day) reduces sales; historical data shows ~15% drop for similar closures. Price increase to $10.81 (5.5% above regular) likely suppresses demand—past week at same price sold 31 units (12% below baseline). No promotion, event, or seasonal ramp. The classical model's 1.00 is misleading: it ignores the price effect and closure. Evidence for price effect is moderate (1 data point at same price), so shrink toward 1.0. Closure effect is supported by past patterns. Combine multiplicatively, shrink uncertainty.

brief:
PRODUCT: AA Batteries 8-pack | category Household | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-10-12 to 2026-10-18 (next week)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 10.81 (+5.5% vs regular price 10.25)
  planner notes: Store closed Monday for renovation

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 35.2 | 5%-95%: 20.0 - 56.8 | 10%-90%: 22.2 - 54.0

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-44% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
